Graph hull closure of every subset therefore equals the original closure under the bijection. On a finite set this identifies all convex traces and hence the exact Helly number. The corrected application to the nonzero atomic local weights gives the claimed closed-cap lower bound.

For each graph point contained in the cap, the corresponding fiber trace is a containing continuous halfspace or the whole fiber. Boundary fibers and d=0 thus pay at least t_z. The all-zero local-budget case is trivial.

At a q-dimensional fiber its intrinsic volume is ordinary volume on its affine hull and its full-mass metronoid is its centroid. Lower-dimensional fibers have zero H_q mass and the q=0 fibers are point masses. The monotonicity argument for gamma_q is valid.
